The module has undefined behavior on three unchecked paths, a lock-order deadlock in `Service`, and inventory arithmetic that panics in debug builds and wraps in release builds.

### Memory safety

`SlotTable::lookup` (L185) calls `get_unchecked` on a slot index the comment says comes from a scanner. If `slot >= slots.len()`, that read is undefined behavior.

`append_batch` (L194–L196) takes a raw pointer at the current end of `buf`, then calls `extend_from_slice`. That can reallocate and free the old buffer. The `unsafe` read of `first` is then a use-after-free. The value it wants is already in `head`.

`decode` (L218) runs `from_utf8_unchecked` on bytes the comment says arrived from the network. If those bytes are not UTF-8, constructing a `&str` is undefined behavior. The following `try_into().unwrap()` calls are safe: the length check guarantees those slices are 4 bytes.

### Panics and overflow

In debug builds, overflowing integer arithmetic panics. In release builds it wraps, so quantities and money silently corrupt.

- `Item::available` (L47) does `on_hand - reserved`. Any path that leaves `reserved > on_hand` panics here, including `reserve` and `low_stock`.
- `record_loss` (L120) does `on_hand -= lost` with no check against `on_hand` or `reserved`. A loss larger than `on_hand` underflows, and a smaller loss can still push `on_hand` below `reserved`.
- `ship` (L112) checks `reserved` only. After that invariant is broken, `on_hand -= qty` underflows. `reserved` is already reduced by then, so a panic also leaves the row half-updated.
- `total_value` (L127) can overflow both on `on_hand as u64 * price_cents` and on the `sum()`.
- `deltas` (L156) walks `0..prices.len()` and reads `prices[i + 1]`. For every non-empty slice the last step is out of bounds and panics. An empty slice returns an empty vec. The subtraction (L157) can also overflow `i64` (`i64::MIN - 1`, `i64::MAX - (-1)`).
- `moving_average` (L144) `assert!`s and panics when `window == 0`.
- `next_id` (L250) uses `+= 1`. At `u64::MAX` that panics in debug, or wraps to 0 in release and `HashMap::insert` overwrites an existing hold, leaving its units reserved with no entry.
- `Instant::now() + ttl` (L253) panics if the deadline is not representable. `reserve` has already succeeded, so those units stay reserved and no hold is stored.

### Logic

`receive` (L81) always `insert`s a new `Item` whose `on_hand` is `qty` and whose `reserved` is 0. For an existing SKU this drops the previous on-hand quantity, clears reservations, and replaces the name and price. The doc comment describes adding units to the existing row. Outstanding `Service` holds still refer to the old reservation.

`release` (L101) uses `saturating_sub` and returns `Ok(())` when `qty` is greater than `reserved`. The reservation count shrinks by less than the caller asked, and the caller is told it succeeded. `reserve` and `ship` both report `Insufficient` for the same kind of mismatch.

`encode` (L204) stores `name.len() as u8`. A name longer than 255 bytes is truncated in the length prefix, so `decode` treats later name bytes as the SKU and quantity.

`confirm` (L260) `remove`s the hold before `release` or `ship` has succeeded. If `ship` returns `Insufficient`, the hold is already gone, the units stay in `reserved`, and `sweep_expired` will never see them. The same removal happens before the expired-path `release`, so an error there drops the hold without returning the stock.

### Concurrency

`place_hold` locks `warehouse` and then `holds` (L245, L247). `sweep_expired` uses that same order (L272, L273). `confirm` locks `holds` and then `warehouse` (L259, then L262 or L265). Two threads, one in `confirm` and one in `place_hold` or `sweep_expired`, can each hold one mutex and wait for the other. That deadlock is permanent. `place_hold` may already have reserved the stock.

ISSUES:
L47: available() underflows when reserved > on_hand (debug panic, release wrap)
L81: receive() replaces an existing SKU, resetting on_hand to qty and reserved to 0
L101: release() saturates and returns Ok when qty exceeds reserved
L112: ship() subtracts qty from on_hand without an on_hand check and can underflow
L120: record_loss() subtracts lost from on_hand unchecked and can leave reserved above on_hand
L127: total_value() product and sum can overflow u64
L144: moving_average() panics when window is 0
L156: deltas() indexes prices[i + 1] for every i including the last, panicking on a non-empty slice
L157: deltas() i64 subtraction can overflow
L185: lookup() get_unchecked on an untrusted slot is undefined behavior when out of range
L196: append_batch() dereferences a buf pointer after extend_from_slice may reallocate (use-after-free)
L204: encode() truncates name.len() to u8, corrupting names longer than 255 bytes
L218: decode() from_utf8_unchecked on network bytes is undefined behavior for invalid UTF-8
L250: next_id += 1 overflows u64, panicking or overwriting an existing hold id
L253: Instant::now() + ttl panics on overflow after reserve has already succeeded
L259: confirm() locks holds then warehouse, deadlocking with place_hold and sweep_expired
L260: confirm() removes the hold before ship/release commits, leaking the reservation on failure

Beginning a review of the Rust inventory module for real defects.

Found a potential integer overflow in `Item::available()`. It subtracts `reserved` from `on_hand` without saturating, so if `reserved` exceeds `on_hand`, the result wraps in release mode or panics in debug mode.

`record_loss` can underflow `on_hand` when the loss exceeds available stock. It also fails to check that `on_hand` remains above `reserved`, so after a large loss `reserved` can exceed `on_hand` and trigger the same overflow in `available()`.

`receive()` replaces the entire item for an existing SKU instead of adding to the current quantity. This wipes existing stock, reservations, and overwrites the name and price. It also destroys reserved counts, which can desync timed holds.

`release()` silently clamps the quantity to zero when releasing more than reserved. It returns `Ok(())` instead of `Err(Insufficient)`, which `reserve()` and `ship()` return for the same case. This inconsistency can undercount actual holds.

`total_value()` multiplies `on_hand` by `price_cents` and sums the results. Both the per-item product and the total can overflow `u64`, causing a panic in debug mode or silent wrapping in release.

`low_stock()` calls `available()`, so it inherits the same underflow risk. If `available()` panics, `low_stock()` will also panic.

`moving_average` panics via an `assert!` when the window is zero. This is a runtime panic on invalid input rather than a logic error.

The `moving_average` assert is defensive. A zero window would otherwise produce an empty slice and a division by zero. It is acceptable as documented precondition validation.

Now examining `deltas()` for potential issues.

`deltas()` panics on single-element input. The loop `0..prices.len()` reaches `prices[len]`, which is out of bounds. It should use `0..prices.len().saturating_sub(1)` or `1..prices.len()`. The subtraction `prices[i + 1] - prices[i]` can also overflow `i64`.

`SlotTable::lookup()` uses `get_unchecked(slot)`, which is undefined behaviour when the slot index is out of bounds. The comment notes that slot values come from an untrusted handheld scanner, so this is a real memory safety defect. It should use safe indexing instead.

`append_batch()` computes a pointer with `buf.as_ptr().wrapping_add(start)` after pushing the head element. This is unsafe and can produce an invalid pointer if the vector reallocation occurs.

`encode()` silently truncates item names longer than 255 bytes by casting `name.len()` to `u8`. The decoder then reads the wrong length, corrupting the SKU and quantity fields or producing malformed output.

`decode()` uses `std::str::from_utf8_unchecked` on raw network bytes. This is undefined behaviour if the payload contains invalid UTF-8.

`decode()` should use `from_utf8` and return `Malformed` instead of `from_utf8_unchecked`.

`Service::place_hold()` locks the warehouse, then holds, then next_id. This lock ordering could deadlock against other methods that acquire those same locks in a different sequence.

`confirm()` locks `holds` before `warehouse`, while `sweep_expired()` locks `warehouse` before `holds`. This ABBA ordering guarantees a deadlock between any thread holding one lock and another holding the other.

The `next_id` counter increments without saturating. After `2^64` holds, it wraps to zero in release mode or panics in debug mode. Duplicate IDs would then overwrite existing holds in the HashMap, silently dropping reservations while stock remains reserved.

`Instant::now() + ttl` can panic if the TTL is large enough to overflow `Instant`. The code should use `checked_add` instead.

`place_hold` leaves stock reserved if `Instant::now() + ttl` panics, because the hold record is never inserted. The `next_id` counter starts at 1, which is fine.

`confirm()` removes the hold before checking expiration. If the hold is expired, it releases stock back to the warehouse and returns an error. This is safe because the hold record is already gone from the map.

`confirm()` removes the hold from the map before checking expiry or calling `ship()`. If `release()` fails because the SKU was wiped by `receive()`, or if `ship()` fails due to a mismatched reservation count, the hold record is already gone and the stock reservation may be orphaned.

`confirm()` removes the hold before checking expiry or calling `ship()`. If `ship()` fails, the hold record is already gone and the caller cannot retry. The stock state may also be inconsistent with the removed hold.

When a hold expires, `confirm()` releases stock while still holding the `holds` lock, then tries to acquire the `warehouse` lock. This reverses the lock order used by other methods and can deadlock.

`record_loss` can leave `reserved` above `on_hand`. If `on_hand` is then reduced further, `available()` panics in debug mode. `ship()` also panics on the same underflow because it subtracts from `on_hand` without first checking that `on_hand` is sufficient.

`reserve()` panics via `available()` when `reserved` exceeds `on_hand`, rather than returning an error. This is a logic defect.

`append_batch()` computes an unsafe pointer with `buf.as_ptr().wrapping_add(start)` after pushing the head element. This is unnecessary because the first SKU is already known as `head`. The real defect is the undefined behaviour from using that raw pointer.

`append_batch()` creates a raw pointer after pushing the head element, then mutates the vector with `extend_from_slice`. If reallocation occurs, the pointer becomes dangling, which is undefined behaviour. The code must be correct for all paths, not just the common case where capacity suffices.

`confirm()` removes the hold from the map before calling `ship()`. If `ship()` panics or fails, the hold record is already gone and the stock reservation may be orphaned. This is a remove-before-commit defect.

`confirm()` also holds the `holds` lock while acquiring the `warehouse` lock in both the expired and success paths, which creates a lock ordering problem.

`sweep_expired` ignores errors from `release` inside the `holds.retain` closure. If a SKU is unknown, reserved stock is not updated and the hold record is removed.

`place_hold` reserves stock before incrementing `next_id`. If the counter panics while holding the lock, the reservation is orphaned because the hold record was never inserted.

`receive` replaces an existing SKU entirely instead of adding to `on_hand`. It also resets `reserved` to zero and overwrites the price and name. This violates the documented additive semantics and destroys reservation accounting.

`total_value` can panic in debug mode or wrap in release mode when `on_hand` multiplied by `price_cents` exceeds `u64::MAX`, and `.sum()` on the resulting iterator also overflows. `Item::available` panics on underflow when `reserved` exceeds `on_hand`. `record_loss` subtracts without bounds checking, which can panic or wrap. `ship` assumes `on_hand` is sufficient without verifying it, so an invariant violation from `record_loss` causes a panic.

`release()` silently saturates the reserved count when the requested release exceeds available stock. This corrupts reservation accounting and desynchronizes the warehouse state.

`parse_command` accepts a quantity of zero, which is valid and not a defect.

`deltas()` contains an off-by-one panic and an integer overflow on subtraction.

`deltas()` always panics on non-empty input because its loop index reaches `len` and accesses `prices[len]`. `moving_average()` returns an empty vector when the window size exceeds the slice length.

`deltas()` panics when the window is zero. A window larger than `2^53` causes precision loss in `moving_average()` because `usize` cannot be exactly represented as `f64`; this is a minor issue and not a defect.

`receive` zeroes `reserved` without releasing the existing holds. Those holds remain in the map, so `confirm` and `ship` see zero reserved stock and fail with `Insufficient`. The hold record is orphaned until `confirm` removes it.

`low_stock` relies on `available()` for filtering and sorting. If `record_loss` corrupts the count, a wrapped underflow makes the value huge, so the low-stock check is bypassed.

`lookup` returns `None` for empty slots but uses `get_unchecked` for out-of-bounds indices, which is undefined behaviour instead of returning `None`.

`append_batch` returns the first SKU via a raw pointer instead of the known `head` value. This is unnecessary and unsafe if the pointer becomes dangling.

`next_id` wraps around, so `holds.insert` can overwrite an existing hold record and corrupt reservation accounting.

`record_loss` does not check whether `on_hand` is sufficient to cover the reserved count before deducting, so it can remove units that are still held by active reservations.

`sweep_expired` mutably borrows the warehouse while calling `holds.retain`, which can cause a borrow checker conflict.

The `sweep_expired` borrow concern was unfounded. The closure captures the warehouse reference by value, so it does not conflict with the mutable borrow of the holds map.

A panic in `confirm` while holding the `holds` lock poisons that mutex, so other threads will panic on their next `unwrap`. This is a secondary effect of the underflow bug.

`encode` and `decode` omit the `price_cents` field, so the wire format is incomplete.

The wire format comment explicitly omits price and reserved, so omitting those fields is correct relative to the spec. The `as u8` cast truncates the name length when it exceeds 255 bytes; if the truncated value happens to be short enough, decoding succeeds with corrupted data. `from_utf8_unchecked` remains undefined behaviour for invalid UTF-8 even when the length is valid.

The `moving_average` sum can overflow if the window exceeds `2^32` elements, but this is practically impossible. The `total_value` overflow is realistic and will be included.

I am reconsidering whether `moving_average` should be listed. It panics on a documented invalid input, but library assertions for broken preconditions are often treated as design choices rather than real defects.

`moving_average` panics on a documented invalid input, so it will be listed as a panic defect. `release` deliberately clamps over-releases with `saturating_sub`, but returns `Ok` anyway, so callers believe the full quantity was released.

`parse_command` is correct and has no bugs. The `Hold` struct exposes its `expires` field as public, so callers can mutate it directly.

Multiple holds on the same SKU are not tracked individually. The code reserves and releases quantities globally, so overlapping reservations for one item cannot be distinguished.

`encode` can panic when the name length exceeds `usize::MAX`, because `1 + name.len()` overflows before the vector is allocated.

`receive` can itself break the `available()` invariant. If the new quantity is smaller than the existing reserved count, the old reservations are cleared while the hold records remain in the Service map. `confirm` then sees zero reserved stock and fails to ship, leaving those holds orphaned.

`append_batch` dereferences a raw pointer into `buf` after `extend_from_slice`, which may reallocate and cause use-after-free or undefined behavior. `Instant::now() + ttl` panics when the TTL overflows the instant, leaving the hold record orphaned.

`confirm` removes the hold record before `ship` or `release` succeeds, so a failed ship leaves stock permanently reserved. `confirm` also acquires the `holds` lock before the warehouse lock, which deadlocks with `place_hold` and `sweep_expired` because they acquire the locks in the opposite order.

I will lead with the defects rather than contrast them. I am considering compiling the tests to verify panics and undefined behavior.

`sweep_expired` drops the result of `release`, so a failed release leaves stock permanently reserved. This is not a separate defect because `release` only ever fails on an unknown SKU, and after a `receive` overwrite the SKU still exists.

`record_loss` returns `Result` but never yields `Insufficient`, and it subtracts the loss with `-=` which panics when the loss exceeds available stock. `ship` also panics on underflow after returning `Insufficient`. The `moving_average` loop is sound.

Reconsidering whether `moving_average` panics when the window exceeds the slice length. In Rust, `RangeInclusive` construction does not panic on invalid bounds; iteration simply yields nothing. This means the function may return an empty vector rather than crashing.

`RangeInclusive` panics during iteration when the end value is the maximum value of the type. This means `moving_average` can crash if the window equals or exceeds the slice length.

The `moving_average` panic is unreachable. Slice lengths are bounded by `isize::MAX`, so the window can never equal `usize::MAX` and the inclusive range will not overflow.

`place_hold` inserts the hold record into the map only after `reserve` succeeds, so a failed reservation leaves no hold entry at all.

`next_id` wraps around on overflow, so `holds.insert` can overwrite an existing hold record and corrupt reservation accounting. The `u64` counter increment in debug mode panics while all three locks are held.

`release` and `ship` both subtract quantities with plain `-=` without checking for underflow, so they panic when the reserved or on-hand count is smaller than requested. `record_loss` also uses plain `-=` and panics if the loss exceeds available stock. The `moving_average` loop overflows its index because it accesses `prices[i + 1]` while iterating from zero to `prices.len() - 1`, which is out of bounds.

`total_value()` and `deltas()` compute sums with unchecked u64 and i64 arithmetic, so they can silently wrap. `SlotTable::lookup()` uses `get_unchecked` on an untrusted slot index, which is undefined behavior when the index is out of range.
